text.p: NARODNA OBRODA - The Constitutional Court is expected to rule on Wednesday on the question of whether the constitution can changed by a referendum.
- The government on Tuesday approved a draft amendment to the securities law which, if approved by parliament, will allow trading with foreign securities on the Slovak capital market.
- April CPI stood at 0.5 percent against the previous month, putting prices up 6.5 percent year-on-year.
- The Supreme Court ruled on Tuesday that the police should not return the passport of Michal Kovac Junior, son of President Michal Kovac, due to allegations of financial fraud.
- Vahostav a.s., one of Slovakia's largest construction firms, said it expected a net profit of around 97 million crowns in 1997.
- Private bank Istrobanka posted a pre-tax profit of 100.7 million crowns in 1996, a 35 percent increase over the previous year.

- Czech car maker Skoda sold a record 3,147 units in Slovakia in April. Skoda plans to export some 25,000 cars in 1997, while the volume of Slovakia's deliveries for Skoda production should total some 3.8 billion crowns this year.

PRAVDA - Prime Minister Vladimir Meciar and the leader of strongest opposition party the Christian Democratic Movement (KDH), Jan Carnogursky, met on Tuesday to discuss problems related to the upcoming referendum on direct presidential elections.
- Meciar and Carnogursky said their parties would respect the ruling of the Constitutional Court on changes to the constitution by referendum.

- Meciar's ruling Movement for a Democratic Slovakia (HZDS) will propose round table talks with all parliamentary parties after the referenda on NATO membership and presidential elections. HZDS said it could support attempts to approve the direct presidential election through a constitutional majority in parliament.
- A group of HZDS deputies has proposed a draft law calling for earlier general elections next summer.
- Parliament on Tuesday approved the first reading of an increase in pensions by 10 percent, effective July 1, 1997.
- Parliament also approved the first reading of a draft law banning privatisation of the second terrestrial channel of the public Slovak Television (STV).

SME - Two minor coalition parties, the ultra right Slovak National Party (SNS) and the extreme-left Workers Party, have so far not presented a draft resolution asking the Russian Federation to guarantee Slovakia's neutrality.
- Economics Minister Karol Cesnek said demands by the state-run electric monopoly Slovenske Elektrarne for a 50 percent increase in energy prices was "excessive".
HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - The National Bank of Slovakia posted a profit of 3.5 billion crowns in 1996, the lowest profit in its three-year history.
- The balance sum of Slovakia's largest savings bank Slovenska Sporitelna totalled 172.8 billion crowns in 1996, accounting for 22 percent of the local banking sector.
